idiom_name: scala.collection.immutable persistent values + AtomicReference/@volatile publication (or j.u.c.CopyOnWriteArrayList)
implementation_notes: Scala's standard library already separates the two roles the pattern needs: a collection in scala.collection.immutable 'is guaranteed to be immutable for everyone ... accessing the same collection value repeatedly at different points in time will always yield a collection with the same elements', and updates return a new collection instead of touching the old one - copy-on-write done with structural sharing instead of a reference-counted body. Publication is then an AtomicReference with compareAndSet/updateAndGet, or a @volatile field written by a single owner, read once into a local by readers. On the JVM, java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList remains the right tool when the snapshot is a list read far more often than written. The counted body itself is never written by hand; the GC owns the count.
pitfalls: Immutable is not thread-safe by itself: a compound read-modify-write on the AtomicReference (get, compute, set) races unless it uses updateAndGet/compareAndSet, and assigning to a plain @volatile var is not a CAS.

Structural sharing keeps copies cheap but not free: each update rebuilds the path to the changed node, so pick the collection by write pattern - and beware of import scala.collection.mutable shadowing the immutable defaults, which silently changes what a type means.

Nested mutability defeats the snapshot: case classes with var fields or mutable collections inside the snapshot are shared with every reader - the immutability guarantee stops at the snapshot's own structure.
sources: Scala documentation, Mutable and Immutable Collections - scala.collection.immutable collections 'never change' and updates 'return a new collection and leave the old collection unchanged': https://docs.scala-lang.org/overviews/collections-2.13/overview.html

Java SE 21 API, CopyOnWriteArrayList - the JVM collection used for read-mostly snapshot lists from Scala: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/CopyOnWriteArrayList.html
